Close painted still life in a dark timber grain room at night, low angle. A round, full-bellied earthenware water jar has overflowed: water spills over its wet lip and runs down its curved belly in glistening streams into a spreading pool on the packed earth. Behind it two hemp grain sacks lie crushed flat, pressed into the shape of two bodies, split open, millet spilled everywhere and scattered as if kicked. A length of dusty-rose #e8a04a silk lies crumpled in the wet, a red #e8563f cord tangled through it. An oil lamp burned down to one last glowing bead. Warm low lamp key against crushed umber dark. Spent, drenched, satisfied afterglow. PAINTED STILL — no people, no figures, no faces, no hands anywhere in the frame; the place or object IS the subject. Openly erotic metaphor: the shapes, wetness, swelling, thrusting and release unmistakably read as bodies and sex, the way a frank erotic painting does — yet everything stays landscape and object, no nudity, no literal anatomy. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). Hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL: granulated wet-in-wet washes and broken-colour dabs for sky, water and stone, dry-brush texture, soft bleeding edges and a faint paper grain; oil glazes deepen the darks and a touch of impasto lands on the single brightest highlight. Romantic-painting layout: one bold shape, at least half the frame quiet negative space, distant detail dissolving into haze. Film tenebrism: one hard directional key (sun, moon or lamp) against big dark masses, a thin edge of real light along the subject, painted bokeh from small real lights. Beautiful, luminous, painterly. NOT photoreal, NOT 3D, NOT a cartoon. No text. No watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
